body.target_estimand: \(\tau_P(0)\), defined exclusively as the value at zero of the unique continuous extension of \(\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\)

sampling_model.design: Known exactly uniform random design on \([0,1]^d\) with \(n\) independent observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is strictly positive almost everywhere and equals zero only at \(x=0\) when \(\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P\), \(e_P\), \(\mu_{0,P}\), or \(\tau_P\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give a pointwise H\"older-CATE nuisance-smoothness frontier under bounded overlap, with the lower construction of Definition 1 using a covariate density supported on a perforated set.
Theorem 3 bounds a local-polynomial R-learner under bounded estimated propensities and nondegenerate local Gram matrices.
Theorem 2.1 controls the affinity between two convex mixtures when perturbations localize to a measurable partition.
The random-design variance-functional results use local polynomial U-statistics and a fuzzy lower construction to expose a regression-functional elbow.
Theorem 1 analyzes empirical-Gram higher-order influence-function corrections that remove a covariate-density smoothness requirement for average doubly robust functionals.
Theorem 2 gives near-minimax integrated \(L_1\) rates for random treated and control designs under bounded density ratios and contrast smoothness at most one.
Theorem 1 gives the scalar pointwise regression rate under a regularly varying design density through a local-mass balance.
The weak-overlap results derive thresholded average-effect limit laws and a scalar regression smoothness degradation under propensity-tail restrictions.
Corollary 4 gives pointwise RKHS CATE rates without consistent propensity estimation while retaining a uniform positive overlap parameter.

body.tldr: The target is the sharp mean-absolute minimax risk for \(\tau_P(0)\) when treatment probability vanishes as \(\lVert x\rVert_{\infty}^{\kappa}\) and its H\"older multiplier is unknown. The paper must derive every power and critical logarithm, give a total Gram-stabilized higher-order local-polynomial R-estimator, prove a matching full-support Bernoulli lower bound on the exactly uniform design, and characterize exactly when supplying the propensity changes the rate. The oracle rate and a sufficient oracle-attainment region are supporting results; neither substitutes for the full frontier.

project_justification.gap: The closest pointwise CATE minimax theorem assumes bounded overlap and uses a support-modified fuzzy lower construction; weak-overlap work instead treats average effects or scalar regression, and recent propensity-free pointwise RKHS theory retains a global overlap lower bound.
project_justification.niche: Exactly uniform covariates and a known polynomial overlap geometry isolate a local treatment-scarcity experiment in which the contrast is smoother than a rough baseline and the unknown multiplier may create a separate nuisance frontier.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a same-class matched minimax rate, an oracle-versus-unknown phase diagram, all critical logarithms, a total finite-operation estimator, and a full-support fixed-\(n\) Bernoulli product-mixture converse.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Theorems 1--2 and Definition 1, supplies the closest bounded-overlap pointwise contrast frontier and the localized fuzzy-hypothesis narrative. At \(\kappa=0\), Theorem 3 recovers its polynomial rate on the narrower singleton uniform design while requiring a new legal full-support converse because the comparator's displayed density removes nuisance-bump transition regions; at \(\kappa>0\), the corner-zero experiment lies outside its bounded-overlap class. Kennedy2023DRCATE, Theorem 3 and Corollary 4, supplies the local-polynomial R-equation and oracle-efficiency motivation under bounded propensities and stable Gram matrices. RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, supplies the two-convex-mixture affinity method whose partition-local step must be rebuilt for overlapping smooth compensation. ShenGaoWittenHan2020 supplies the closest random-design local-polynomial U-statistic and regression-functional lower-bound geometry. LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF supplies empirical projection kernels and the exact lesson that Gram estimation can replace an unnecessary density-smoothness requirement. GaoHan2020, Theorem 2, gives random-design integrated contrast rates with scarcity asymmetry but not pointwise loss on one exactly uniform law. Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign, Theorem 1, gives the local-mass oracle regression benchmark under a design zero. Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics derives weak-overlap average-effect limit laws and scalar-regression rates rather than the smoother pointwise contrast hidden behind two unknown nuisances. Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE, Corollary 4, gives pointwise rates without propensity consistency in an RKHS model with a positive global overlap constant. WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the consumer: the implemented workflow learns nuisance regressions, uses R-learner residualization, and warns that treatment imbalance undermines local effect estimation.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The full-support squared-frame algebra cancels the one-observation Bernoulli mixtures, but a shared Rademacher prior creates nonzero two-observation cross terms. The first admissibility test is therefore the one-dimensional bounded-overlap rough-nuisance branch \(d=1\), \(\kappa=0\), and \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma/(2\gamma+1)\). For noninteger \(\kappa<\beta\) in one dimension, exact deterministic-contrast cancellation can also violate baseline H\"older regularity; for \(d\ge2\), max-norm tie surfaces obstruct naive compensation when smoothness exceeds one. These facts are diagnostics, not theorem contributions, and the product-mixture, corner-taper, and tie-smoothing steps remain part of Open-ended Question 2.
body.honest_scope: The oracle rate and the three-block upper inequality are supporting claims to establish. The full unknown-multiplier frontier, its higher-order estimator, every nuisance-critical logarithm, and the fixed-uniform product-mixture converse are open. Stage 0 begins with the legal full-support Bernoulli product-mixture test at \(d=1\), \(\kappa=0\), and \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma/(2\gamma+1)\); the full phase diagram is conditional on resolving that test. The explicit sanity reduction is Theorem 3: at \(\kappa=0\), the exact-uniform class recovers the bounded-overlap polynomial rate with no critical logarithm through a new same-class converse rather than the published perforated-support witness.
